newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: PRESS DIGEST - Bangladesh Newspapers - Nov 20.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Bangladesh Newspapers - Nov 20.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Bangladesh press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina has said she will welcome any initiative by President Shahabuddin Ahmed for a dialogue between ruling Awami League and main opposition Bangladesh Nationalist Party (BNP) to resolve an impasse arising from the latter's boycott of parliament.
BNP chief Begum Khaleda Zia, former prime minister, has said her party legislators are just abstaining from attending parliament, but have not boycotted it.
Home Minister Rafiqul Islam has appealed to people of all strata including political parties, professionals and the press for launching a concerted crusade to free the country from terrorism.
A seminar organised by Japan and ESCAP in Tokyo has recommended identification of the missing links of the grand road plan connecting the capitals of Asian countries.
State Minister for Law Abdul Matin Khasru has said the killers of Bangabandhu Sheikh Mujibur Rahman will be tried as per law of the land after the scrapping of the indemnity ordinance by parliament.
Finance Minister S.A.M.S. Kibria said economic reforms, infrastructure facilities and political stability have now set the stage for direct foreign investment (DFI) in Bangladesh.
Finance Minister S.A.M.S. Kibria said on Tuesday the government is determined to play its due role in streamlining the growth pattern of the country's capital market.
A meeting of the members of Dhaka Stock Exchange (DSE) have expressed their anguish over some of the regulatory steps taken by the Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC).
